llmJudgeRequirements.description: Must define auth screens in createNativeStackNavigator static config using screen-level `if` hooks (e.g., signed-in screens vs signed-out screens).
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: createNativeStackNavigator is called with a static config object; Login has `if: useIsSignedOut` and Home has `if: useIsSignedIn`, exactly matching the screen-level `if` hook pattern.
evidence: const Stack = createNativeStackNavigator({ screens: { Login: { if: useIsSignedOut, screen: LoginScreen }, Home: { if: useIsSignedIn, screen: HomeScreen } } })

llmJudgeRequirements.description: Must maintain authentication state and derive route availability from that state (signed in/out conditions).
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: `isSignedIn` boolean in App's useState is the sole auth state; `useIsSignedIn` and `useIsSignedOut` derive from it via AuthContext, and screen availability is derived from those hooks.
evidence: const useIsSignedIn = () => { const { isSignedIn } = useAuthContext(); return isSignedIn }

llmJudgeRequirements.description: After successful login, Home must become the active available route and Login must no longer be available.
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: Pressing 'Sign in' calls `signIn` which sets `isSignedIn` to true; this makes `useIsSignedIn` return true (Home's `if` guard passes) and `useIsSignedOut` return false (Login's `if` guard fails), so Home becomes the only available route.

llmJudgeRequirements.description: After successful login, back navigation must not return to Login.
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: When `isSignedIn` becomes true, the Login screen is removed from the navigator entirely via its `if: useIsSignedOut` guard. React Navigation's static `if`-guard mechanism removes the screen from the stack, so there is no Login entry to navigate back to.

llmJudgeRequirements.description: Must not imperatively navigate to Home/SignIn for core auth transition when using `if`-guarded routes; route switch should occur from auth state change.
llmJudgeRequirements.reason: No `navigation.navigate`, `navigation.replace`, `router.push`, or any other imperative navigation call is present in the file. Auth transition is driven purely by state change causing `if` guards to re-evaluate.
evidence: No navigation.navigate or similar calls found anywhere in the file
